title: French invasion of Russia
summary: Napoleon's Grande Armée entered Russia in 1812 and retreated from Moscow from 19 October. Cold, disease and fighting destroyed it; an estimated 612,000 combatants entered and only 112,000 returned. The loss of trained men and cavalry weakened France, and Prussia then changed sides in 1813.

as_recorded.value: Napoleon began his retreat, his army now 110,000 strong, on October 19, 1812

where.modern_name: Moscow, Russia (proxy pin: the invasion reached Moscow and the retreat began there; the route ran from the Neman)

importance.justification: The destruction of Napoleon's Grande Armée reshaped the Napoleonic Wars and European alliances.

audience_note: Describes very heavy military deaths, disease and suffering of prisoners and wounded.

sources.title: Evidence for Louse-Transmitted Diseases in Soldiers of Napoleon’s Grand Army in Vilnius | The Journal of Infectious Diseases | Oxford Academic

reviewer_note: Sources cover mainly the retreat; neither gives the June invasion date, so the start is only the year 1812. The second source is a disease study that only supports the disease claim. Casualty figures are estimates. (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from Encyclopaedia Britannica, Oxford University Press; quotes machine-checked.)
